status: author draft after critic and verifier-fix rounds, pending re-verification

confidence_legend.H: consistent systematic reviews or an official standard
confidence_legend.M: meta-analysis with limitations or several concordant studies
confidence_legend.L: single/small studies, conflicting results, or design inference without direct evidence

kind_legend.evidence: value taken from the cited study or guideline
kind_legend.design_inference: engineering default chosen by the report author; not a study result

parameters.name: weekly_dose_adult
parameters.notes: WHO-ITU H.870 Mode 1; implement as running weekly dose meter with warnings.

parameters.name: weekly_dose_sensitive
parameters.notes: WHO-ITU H.870 Mode 2; offer as user-selectable safer mode.

parameters.name: equal_energy_rule
parameters.value: 100 dB for 16 min = 80 dB for 40 h
parameters.notes: Example given in the WHO-ITU standard is 100 dB for 16 min; own calculation from the 1.6 Pa2h definition gives about 24 min at 100 dB (p=2 Pa, p2=4 Pa2, 1.6/4=0.4 h). Use the dose definition, not the worked example. Each +3 dB halves allowed time (equal-energy principle; derived, not quoted).

parameters.name: leisure_noise_yearly_average
parameters.notes: Conditional WHO Europe 2018 recommendation for all leisure sources combined.

parameters.name: loudness_calibration
parameters.value: per-device output calibration or conservative default
parameters.notes: Gap: no study found gives target levels in LUFS or headphone norms for focus/relax/sleep; studies report dB SPL at the ear. In-app levels are an engineering decision; safety is bounded by the WHO-ITU weekly dose in dB SPL, which needs per-device output calibration.

parameters.name: epilepsy_screen
parameters.value: warning + opt-out for rhythmic/gamma stimulation if seizure history
parameters.notes: 40 Hz trials excluded seizure history; no human data on seizures triggered by binaural beats or AM music found (gap, not proof of safety).

parameters.name: tinnitus_monitoring
parameters.value: ask about tinnitus after gamma/40 Hz sessions
parameters.notes: Meta-analysis in AD/MCI: tinnitus RR 6.46 (p=0.08), RD 0.16 (p=0.01).

focus.summary: Instrumental music by default, moderate level; optional ADHD profile with 16 Hz AM music or white/pink noise. No efficacy claims for binaural beats or 40 Hz.

parameters.name: vocals
parameters.value: none (instrumental)
parameters.notes: Lyrics impaired verbal/visual memory and reading (d about -0.3, PMID:37152835); in an RCT with 102 people lyrics worsened an attention/concentration test (PMID:22523045); instrumental lo-fi neutral.

parameters.name: tempo_loudness_combo
parameters.value: avoid fast AND loud simultaneously
parameters.notes: Reading comprehension fell below silence only in fast/high-intensity condition.

parameters.name: base_music_tempo
parameters.notes: Tempo of music used in the AM study; not tested as an independent factor. Faster tempo raises arousal (DOI:10.1525/mp.2002.20.2.151).

parameters.name: am_rate
parameters.notes: Only 16 Hz (beta) vs 8 and 32 Hz tested; benefit only for higher ASRS scores, interaction p=0.048, eta_p2=0.048; company-affiliated authors (PMID:41974870). Range = beta band as defined by the authors; only 16 Hz tested. Experiment 1 analysed 83/160 participants (52% passed screening); volume self-set online and used as covariate. Brain.fm-sponsored RCT NCT05291832 (n=329, completed 2022-07-19) has no posted results. Background music did not change ANT reaction times in children with ADHD (PMID:39024557).

parameters.name: am_alignment
parameters.value: phase-locked to metrical grid (16 Hz = 32nd notes at 120 BPM)
parameters.notes: Keeps modulation musically coherent.

parameters.name: am_spectral_band
parameters.value: low-mid frequencies; little modulation in highs
parameters.notes: Broadband modulation interacted badly with sparse high-frequency events (aesthetic choice in the study).

parameters.name: am_depth
parameters.value: subtle, user-adjustable; start low and ramp
parameters.notes: Depth manipulation had no significant effect; deep modulation degrades aesthetics/distracts. Gradual depth increase was used for acclimatisation in a 40 Hz AM study. Default/range are author defaults, not study values.

parameters.name: am_target_population
parameters.value: opt-in for ADHD/inattention profile
parameters.notes: Effect covaried with self-reported ADHD symptoms; no independent replication.

parameters.name: noise_for_adhd
parameters.value: white or pink noise, opt-in
parameters.confidence: M (children and college-age students, laboratory tasks); L for older adults (extrapolation)
parameters.notes: g=0.249 in children/students with ADHD or high symptoms (laboratory tasks); g=-0.212 without ADHD; no brown-noise studies; adults beyond college age not included. Inattentive profile may benefit, hyperactive-impulsive may worsen (PMID:39583636).

parameters.name: noise_level_reference_adhd
parameters.value: 80 dB (allowed down to 70 dB) in children
parameters.notes: Lab study in children; do not copy as app default.

parameters.name: noise_level_default
parameters.notes: 45 dB white noise improved sustained attention vs office ambient; 65 dB raised stress. Range is author default within WHO weekly dose.

parameters.name: noise_color
parameters.value: no evidence-based preference (white/pink/brown)
parameters.notes: No pupil-linked arousal difference; offer as user preference only.

parameters.name: binaural_beats
parameters.value: not a focus feature; optional texture only
parameters.notes: Inconsistent EEG entrainment; large home study showed slight decline at 15/20 Hz; 16 Hz no consistent sustained-attention benefit. Pilot RCT in 20 children/adolescents with ADHD: no group differences on TOVA or Color Trails; double-blind replication showed no theta increase (PMID:12722933).

parameters.name: binaural_carrier_if_used
parameters.value: low carrier
parameters.notes: Studies used 340-400 Hz; binaural 40 Hz ASSR undetectable above 3 kHz; responses larger at 250 than 1000 Hz.

parameters.name: rhythmic_modulation_type
parameters.value: if rhythmic modulation is used, prefer acoustic (monaural/isochronic/AM) over binaural
parameters.notes: Acoustic beats give larger ASSR than binaural (binaural 40 Hz ASSR vanishes above 3 kHz carriers); isochronic-inspired stimulus raised EEG gamma power more than gamma BB in a 4-min study (n=28). Behavioural BB vs MB results are inconsistent: no difference in one study (n=24), fewer errors with BB but more with MB vs pink noise in another (n=25). No behavioural evidence that either improves focus.

parameters.name: gamma_40hz
parameters.value: do not market for focus
parameters.notes: Mixed/null cognitive results in healthy adults. Two studies by the same first author disagree (no memory effect vs WM improvement). Gamma responses are individual (30-60 Hz) and relate to processing speed rather than inhibitory control (PMID:36675687).

parameters.name: break_music
parameters.value: positive-valence (preferably slow) music during breaks
parameters.notes: Reduced misses after SART break (n=89).

parameters.name: session_timing
parameters.value: start audio before the task; effects of AM were strongest early in session
parameters.notes: BB meta-regression: exposure before task and longer exposure better; AM music benefit only when experienced early.

relax.summary: Listener-preferred slow music, optional breathing pacer at about 6/min that adapts from the user's current rate; sessions up to about 30 min.

parameters.name: music_selection
parameters.value: listener-selected or preference-matched
parameters.notes: Participant-selected music improved HRV more than standardized music; preference moderates stress reduction in a meta-analysis of music alone or with music-assisted relaxation (d=0.67, 22 studies).

parameters.name: expected_effect_stress
parameters.value: d=0.38 physiological, d=0.545 psychological, heart rate d=0.456
parameters.notes: 104 RCTs.

parameters.name: session_length
parameters.notes: Short interventions (<=30 min) particularly effective for HFnu; lower bound is author default.

parameters.name: tempo
parameters.value: slow; include pauses
parameters.notes: Faster tempo raises HR/ventilation, pause lowers them; 60-80 BPM range comes from a narrative review on sleep music.

parameters.name: breathing_pacer_rate
parameters.notes: 0.1 Hz raises LF-HRV; slow breathing (<10/min) raises vagal HRV; no robust effect on stress reactivity. Range is author default around 6/min.

parameters.name: breathing_pacer_adaptation
parameters.value: start at user's measured rate, step down gradually
parameters.notes: With a fixed 6/min pacer participants averaged about 12/min.

parameters.name: breathing_cue_mapping
parameters.value: map inhale/exhale to gentle swell/fade of a pad or noise layer
parameters.notes: No study found comparing audio pacer designs; pure design choice.

parameters.name: monaural_beats_example
parameters.notes: Beats+music reduced anxiety (d=-0.58) but no music-only arm; authors employed by Universal Music Group. Effect cannot be attributed to beats.

parameters.name: binaural_for_anxiety
parameters.value: no claim; heterogeneous clinical evidence
parameters.notes: Perioperative SMD -1.38 vs blank (I2 91.6%), -1.01 vs non-BB audio (I2 95.4%).

parameters.name: white_noise_option
parameters.value: allowed as relaxation background
parameters.notes: Highest HRV among tested 3-min fragments (n=242).

parameters.name: bass_emphasis
parameters.value: no boost by default
parameters.notes: No evidence bass relaxes; high-frequency amplified music gave better HFnu recovery in 12 women; 40 Hz vibroacoustic not different from placebo. Low-frequency-dominant noise at 40 dBA was rated more annoying and attenuated cortisol decline in noise-sensitive people; LFN at 50/70 dBA increased test speed vs silence (arousal), i.e. bass-heavy sound may be arousing rather than relaxing.

sleep.summary: Pre-sleep music 25-60 min with fade-out; masking noise only on demand and quiet; no slow-wave stimulation and no binaural sleep claims.

parameters.name: presleep_music_duration
parameters.notes: Cochrane (adults with insomnia symptoms): PSQI MD -2.79 from 10 studies/708 participants (moderate certainty); objective sleep measures may not improve (3 studies, 136 participants). Default 45 is author choice.

parameters.name: music_features
parameters.value: slower, softer, instrumental, acoustic; allow personal choice
parameters.notes: Descriptive analysis of sleep playlists (loudness d=-1.25, tempo d=-0.47 vs general music); large individual variation.

parameters.name: music_tempo
parameters.value: 60-80 (starting point, not a threshold)
parameters.notes: Narrative review only; no study found that tests this tempo range directly. Sleep playlists also contain faster, louder, more energetic tracks.

parameters.name: music_personalisation
parameters.value: rank sleep tracks by user ratings (comfort, liking, calm) rather than fixed acoustic rules
parameters.notes: Subjective ratings predicted perceived sleep-inducing quality better than musical features; large individual variation in sleep music.

parameters.name: fade_out_timer
parameters.value: default fade-out after sleep onset window
parameters.notes: Design inference. WHO considers mitigating environmental noise in the first part of the night helpful for falling asleep ('is believed'), which is not direct evidence about played sound. All-night pink noise 50 dBA reduced REM by 18.6 min. Timer values are author defaults.

parameters.name: continuous_noise_target_level
parameters.notes: WHO 1999 statement quoted in NNG 2009: continuous noise should not exceed 30 dBA indoors. A narrative otolaryngology review hypothesises maladaptive central auditory plasticity from chronic unstructured white noise even at non-traumatic levels (hypothesis, not RCT evidence).

parameters.name: masking_noise_max_level
parameters.notes: All-night masking OFF by default; offer only as opt-in with a warning. In an RCT, pink noise added to intermittent environmental noise worsened sleep architecture and earplugs were more effective (PMID:41627391); in a 12-person pilot 45 dB pink noise attenuated noise-induced fragmentation (PMID:41513961); 46 dB broadband sound shortened sleep latency (PMID:29312136). Cap is author choice. Consumer infant sleep machines can exceed 85 dBA at maximum volume; enforce a hard output cap.

parameters.name: noise_color_sleep
parameters.value: pink or white by preference; no brown-specific evidence
parameters.notes: Pink-noise studies positive more often (9/11) but low quality; no arousal difference between colors.

parameters.name: binaural_or_monaural_sleep
parameters.value: no efficacy claim
parameters.notes: No sleep-latency difference BB vs MB vs sham at home (n=221); theta BB added nothing to music; 0.25 Hz shortened N2/N3 latency in naps (n=12). Positive sleep findings come from small studies (n=10-24) with silent/no-sound control, so a beat-specific effect cannot be separated from sound per se.

parameters.name: slow_wave_stimulation
parameters.value: disabled (requires at least real-time sleep-stage detection by EEG; phase-locking gives the strongest effect)
parameters.confidence: L-M for evidence; L for the design decision
parameters.notes: In-phase stimulation effective, out-of-phase ineffective; non-phase-locked rhythmic bursts raised delta power only when delivered during EEG-detected slow-wave sleep; random stimulation reduced SWS and memory; memory effect small (g=0.25, p=0.07); effect sizes decline over years, about 34% not blind, memory test-retest reliability near zero; enhanced slow oscillations without memory benefit in a 12-person study.

parameters.name: slow_wave_params_reference_only
parameters.notes: Only for a future EEG-headband integration; not for audio-only mode.

do_not_claim.notes: Several small studies (pilots and RCTs up to about 100 people, three by one group) with inconsistent results, partly without a 440 Hz comparison; a 100-patient dental RCT compared music vs no music only.
Mainly animal studies (rats at 100 dB, zebrafish); one human RCT compared listening to a 528 Hz OM recording with usual care without any sound control.
5 of 14 EEG studies consistent; some show no EEG change.

do_not_claim.claim: 40 Hz improves focus or prevents dementia
do_not_claim.notes: No consistent cognitive benefit; AD trials are device-company funded.

do_not_claim.claim: brown noise is best for ADHD
do_not_claim.notes: No brown-noise studies in the meta-analysis.
